Layer Up: What to Wear at Every Temperature

British weather is unpredictable. This guide shows the ideal gear layers for five temperature zones so you stay comfortable and safe on every ride.

Freezing (Below 5°C)

Heated base layer, thermal mid-layer, winter jacket, winter gloves, neck warmer.

Cold (5–10°C)

Thermal base layer, fleece mid-layer, waterproof jacket, winter gloves.

Mild (10–18°C)

Light base layer, touring jacket with liner, all-season gloves.

Warm (18–25°C)

Mesh base layer, vented jacket, summer gloves.

Hot (25°C+)

Mesh jacket only, summer gloves, hydration pack. Read our Best Motorcycle Roads in Scotland: 15 Must-Ride Routes guide for more. Read our Tyre Wear Patterns: What They Mean guide for more. Read our Motorcycle Glove Buying Guide guide for more. Read our Motorcycle Hand Signals Every Rider Should Know guide for more. Read our What to Do After a Motorcycle Accident guide for more.

Pro Tip: British weather can swing 15 degrees in a day. Always carry one extra layer in your tank bag.
keyTakeaways: The guide splits UK riding into five temperature zones from freezing to hot.
Below 5C calls for a heated base layer, thermals and winter gloves.
Mild 10-18C conditions suit a light base layer and touring jacket with liner.
Above 25C, switch to a mesh jacket and a hydration pack to stay cool.
British weather can swing 15 degrees in a day, so always carry one extra layer.

faq.q: How should I layer for cold-weather motorcycle riding?
faq.a: Use a layering system: a moisture-wicking or heated base layer next to the skin, an insulating mid-layer such as fleece or a thermal, and a windproof, waterproof outer jacket. This traps warm air and lets you add or remove layers as conditions change. Below 5C, heated kit and winter gloves make a big difference.

faq.q: What should I wear riding in hot weather?
faq.a: Above 25C, a mesh jacket that flows air over your body keeps you cool while still offering abrasion and impact protection, paired with ventilated summer gloves. Carry a hydration pack and drink regularly, as dehydration creeps up quickly at speed. Never be tempted to ride in a t-shirt; airflow protection beats bare skin.

faq.q: Why is layering better than one thick jacket?
faq.a: British weather can swing 15 degrees in a single day, and a layering system lets you adapt on the move. Several thinner layers trap more warm air than one bulky garment and can be shed as the day warms up. Always carry one extra layer in your tank bag so a sudden temperature drop does not catch you out.

faq.q: Do I need heated gear for UK winter riding?
faq.a: For sustained riding below 5C, heated base layers, grips or gloves transform comfort and, more importantly, keep your hands functional for safe control. Cold fingers lose dexterity fast, which affects braking and clutch use. If you ride through winter regularly, heated kit is well worth the investment.

faq.q: What should I wear in mild spring or autumn weather?
faq.a: In the 10-18C range, a light base layer under a touring jacket with a removable thermal liner covers most conditions, with all-season gloves on your hands. Keep a waterproof to hand, as showers are common in spring and autumn, and pack an extra thermal in case temperatures drop later in the day.
